claims: Meningococcal vaccines prevent meningitis caused by Neisseria meningitidis bacteria.
Routine meningococcal vaccination is recommended for preteens aged 11-12 years.
MenACWY booster is recommended at age 16.
MenB shots are optional for young adults.
MenB vaccine is recommended for individuals aged 10 or older at high risk.
MenB vaccine is recommended based on shared clinical decision-making for teens and young adults aged 16-23.
Catch-up meningococcal vaccination applies to adolescents aged 13-18 who missed the 11-12 year dose.
Meningococcal vaccination is recommended for younger children and adults with specific health conditions such as asplenia or traveling to high-risk areas.
MenACWY vaccines such as Menactra and Menveo protect against types A, C, W, and Y.
MenB vaccines such as Bexsero and Trumenba protect against serogroup B.
MenABCWY vaccine such as Penbaya combines protection against strains A, B, C, W, and Y in one shot.
Side effects of meningococcal vaccines include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, headache, fever, and fatigue.
Effectiveness for MenB is generally short-term compared to MenACWY.
Boosters are necessary for ongoing risk.
